= Cloud October 2, 2026

[NOTE]
====
Cloud release notes are typically published weekly and summarize changes since the previous publication. Kobiton uses date-based release versioning, with releases identified by the build date in YYMM.DD format. Version information for individual software components is available in the Component versions section.

== Appium Inspector

- *Appium Inspector* in Session Explorer now shows the correct XML hierarchy for each step of iPad automation sessions started without an app, such as a web session in Safari — matching the behavior on iPhone and Android. Previously, these sessions showed the same hierarchy for every step.

// Source: KOB-55247 from PR #662
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/662

== iOS system alerts in automation sessions

- Automation sessions on iOS and iPadOS can now interact with system alerts, such as the alert that asks you to turn on Location Services. Finding a system alert button, reading its `displayed` and `enabled` properties, and clicking it now work as expected. Previously, these commands could fail with a `No active application elements` error.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55247): The Jira impact field describes the fix as covering alerts and
// popups drawn by the iOS system on iPhone and iPad. QA verified the Location Services alert
// only. Confirm that the general "system alerts" wording is acceptable.

// Source: KOB-54722 from PR #653
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/653

== Report access by role

- Access to the *Usage Report* and *Service Level Availability* reports is now based on organization role: ADMIN users can view both reports; MEMBER users cannot.
- Viewing Service Level Availability data now requires the organization management permission.
- All other predefined reports remain visible to everyone in the organization.

// Source: KOB-55245 from PR #651
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/651

== iOS passcode checks

Applies to organizations with passcode mode enabled.

- When an iOS device's test runner fails to start, the device health check now reports the original error instead of a misleading passcode or certificate error. deviceConnect also no longer removes the device passcode when removing it can't resolve the failure.
- iOS devices that aren't supervised by the organization now fail the health check with the reason `Cannot set passcode: the device is not supervised by this organization.` Sessions that request a passcode on these devices fail at session setup. Previously, deviceConnect could set a passcode on these devices that it couldn't remove later.

== Java 17 for exported scripts

- Java Appium scripts exported from Kobiton now use Java 17 and updated Appium and Selenium dependencies for compatibility with current Java frameworks.
- JDK 17 or later is required to build and run newly exported Java projects. Projects exported before this release are unchanged.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-54691): Confirm Standalone availability separately.

// Source: KOB-55195 from PR #646
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/646

== Minimum iOS version raised to 15

Kobiton supports devices running iOS and iPadOS 15 and later. Support for iOS 12, 13, and 14 has been deprecated.

*Highlights*

- Kobiton now rejects devices running iOS 12, 13, or 14 at connection, instead of failing partway through a session. These devices show `UnsupportedOSVersionError` in *Device Management* and can't be used for manual or automation sessions.
- Devices running iOS 15 through iOS 27 continue to support manual and automation sessions.
- After a deviceConnect upgrade, devices running iOS 15 or later come back online automatically.

// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55195): The Jira summary says "Maintenance mode for iOS 12, 13 and 14 support",
// but the description, customer-impact field, and QA results all describe iOS 12-14 devices as
// rejected at connection and unusable. This entry documents the verified behavior (rejected).
// Confirm the intended customer-facing wording with Product before publishing.
//
// REVIEWER NOTE (KOB-55195): The Supported OS versions page and the Prepare an iOS device page
// are updated in the same branch.

// Source: KOB-55058 from PR #645

== License configuration for new deviceConnect deployments

- Starting with *deviceConnect* 2610.1, new deployments require an additional license configuration step before *deviceConnect* can initialize. Existing deployments require no changes.

// Source: KOB-54451 from PR #643
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/643
// Source: KOB-54450 from PR #650
// https://github.com/kobiton/docs/pull/650

== Virtual device visibility in the API

- `GET /v2/devices` now includes available Android emulators and iOS simulators in the `virtual_devices` list. The same filtering, team scoping, and organization access rules used for private devices apply to virtual devices.
- `GET /v2/devices/udid/{udid}` and `GET /v1/devices/{udid}` now return information for virtual devices available to the organization. Previously, these requests returned `404` and `500`, respectively, for available virtual devices.
